title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — active ἥμαρτον ≠ your actual-by-imputation; Pelagius risk
pass_a_gloss: You refuse that reading: Paul, you say, does not write that sin is in all (though the next verse does) but that all sinned, using an active verb for actual sin shared by all—original sin being act only as we sinned in Adam. Your whole edge is that active hemarton means actual sin; the rest beg the start. But an active verb for actual sin means the act of the one who sinned. Show a contrary case, or own that the point helps Pelagius.
pass_b_english: Yet you deny that this satisfies you: for, you say, the Apostle does not say since sin is in all (nay, he says this in the following verse) but, since all have sinned, eph' hoi pantes hemarton, and he uses an active verb, that he may signify actual sin, of which all are partakers. But in original sin we have not sinned by act, except insofar as we sinned in Adam: for when he sinned he sinned for all his posterity, and all men who were born of him sinned in him, because in him all were. The force of proving, if there is any, in those words of yours, consists in this, that the word hemarton, they sinned, being active, signifies actual sin. The rest are petitions of what was in the beginning. And yet that active verb, if it signifies actual sin, surely signifies actual sin committed by him himself who sinned. Bring forward, if you can, a contrary example. See therefore lest this observation of yours favor Pelagius.
source_text: Id tamen negas tibi satisfacere: non enim, inquis, dicit Apostolus quoniam peccatum est in omnibus (immo hoc dicit versu sequente) sed, quoniam omnes peccaverunt, ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον, & utitur verbo activo, ut significet peccatum actuale, cuius omnes sint participes. In peccato autem originali non peccavimus actu, nisi quatenus in Adamo peccavimus: nam cum peccavit pro omnibus suis posteris peccavit, & omnes homines qui ex illo nati sunt in illo peccaverunt, quia in illo omnes fuerunt. Vis probandi, si qua est, in tuis istis verbis, in hoc consistit, quod verbum ἥμαρτον peccaverunt, activum cum sit, significat peccatum actuale. Reliqua petitiones sunt τοῦ ἐν ἀρχῇ. Atqui verbum illud activum, si significat peccatum actuale, profecto peccatum actuale significat ab eo ipso commissum qui peccavit. Profer, si potes, contrarium exemplum. Vide igitur ne haec tua observatio Pelagio faveat.

choices.choice: Active ἥμαρτον means act of the sinner himself; observation risks Pelagius
